claim: A DAF sponsoring organization must be a 170(c) organization (excluding governmental units) that is not a private foundation; banks, trust companies, RIAs, broker-dealers, custodians, for-profit fintechs, insurers, accounting firms and credit unions cannot sponsor DAFs themselves and need an affiliated charity or partner sponsor
notes: Statutory reading; credit-union exemption basis is INFERENCE; not legal advice

claim: Public universities that are governmental units are excluded from sponsoring (170(c)(1)); their affiliated foundations (BMF foundation code 13: 2,919 public-charity entities) can sponsor
Financial institutions that offer DAFs do so through an affiliated or partner sponsor (BofA CGF; Regions-RCF; Wells Fargo-NPT; TIAA-Charityvest; Thrivent Charitable)
Institutional (education/health) DAF sponsors number 165-174 (FY2021-24) holding $3.59bn and ~4,000 accounts; their market share fell from 1.38% to 1.11% of DAF assets
notes: Repo computation from corrected DAFRC panel

claim: Of 3,056 education and health public-charity entities with >= $100M total assets, only 99 show any DAF signal; of T31 community foundations >= $50M, 375 of 394 are already DAFRC sponsors
notes: No signal is not proof of no programme (hosted programmes invisible); hospital assets are operating assets

claim: Community foundations are not a greenfield market for new DAF programmes; growth there requires displacement or hosting
No member-facing credit-union DAF launch was found in 2025-2026 press; CU DAFs remain institutional funds at league foundations (consistent with CLM-024)
Hosted institution programmes on partner sponsors exist (Ohio Wesleyan with The Columbus Foundation; GW and MSU with BNY Mellon CGF, which terminated its DAF programme in Dec 2024)
notes: Post-2024 status of GW/MSU programmes not checked

claim: 12 of 18 university/hospital DAF programme pages state a host minimum (usually 50%), so institutional programmes are host-retention vehicles that need configurable grant-destination rules
Technology is not the binding barrier for most untapped institution types; demand, sponsor status and distribution are
notes: Barrier matrix not validated by interviews

claim: With shared technology, programme-owner break-even is ~3-190 accounts ($0.75-9.5M) when hosted on an existing sponsor, ~8-470 ($2-24M) for an existing charity's own programme, and ~26-1,700 ($6.5-85M) for a newly formed sponsor (base costs; balances $50-250k; fees 0.6-1.5%)
notes: All cost inputs ASSUMPTION ranges; port to F# model

claim: Small-programme viability for the vendor is set by acquisition and onboarding cost: a $10-25k/yr programme cannot repay $60-250k direct CAC within 5 years; only channel/host acquisition at about one year's licence or less works
Small DAF programmes already exist widely (median tail sponsor 24 DAFs; 423 sponsors under $1M), so operating technology is not what prevents small programmes
Employer and embedded DAF channels are occupied (Daffy for Work 2023 and 2026 stock matching; Givinga workplace suite Dec 2025; Morgan Stanley at Work; Benevity; Blackbaud Giving Fund)
From 2026 the OBBBA non-itemizer charitable deduction excludes gifts to DAFs and a 0.5%-of-AGI floor applies to itemizers
notes: Secondary sources; net demand effect unmeasured

claim: Proposed section 4966 regulations (88 FR 77922) were not final in the latest sources found (May-mid 2026) and remain on the 2026-27 priority guidance plan

Land-and-expand within financial institutions is evidenced (nCino ACV net retention 112%; multi-product expansions) but nCino landed with a core workflow platform, not a peripheral data or tooling product

A narrow offering credibly leads to platform adoption only when it is bought by the platform's budget owner, sits on the system-of-record data path, and the vendor survives; new-programme enablement meets this, charity intelligence and migration assessment do not on present evidence
There are 16,544 SEC-registered advisers (YE2025), about two-thirds with under $1bn AUM; median $446.9M
Newly formed sponsor creation (bank, fintech or insurer affiliate) is uneconomic below roughly $7-20M of DAF assets at base costs, so 'sponsor-in-a-box' formation is a weak product
notes: Formation costs (audit, legal, IRS determination time) unmeasured
